anthropic_claude_news.title: Claude Code gets a /design command that lets developers create UI mockups right in the terminal
anthropic_claude_news.summary: Anthropic added a /design command to Claude Code that generates UI mockups as artboards directly in the terminal, before any code is written. Claude reads the existing project for styling cues, so the mockup arrives already matching the app. Automation angle: record a Claude Code /design run end-to-end this week — a terminal-to-mockup clip is the cheapest portfolio proof that you work at the edge of the tool.

anthropic_claude_news.title: Anthropic's per-token cost runs 4.4 times the average on Vercel, and developers keep paying
anthropic_claude_news.summary: Anthropic took 65.1% of Vercel AI Gateway revenue in July while supplying only 30% of tokens processed, meaning its tokens cost roughly 4.4x the platform average. Developers are paying the premium anyway, which says more about agent reliability than about price. Automation angle: build a model-router demo that sends cheap classification to a small model and keeps Claude for the agent loop — cost control is a paid consulting skill.

anthropic_claude_news.title: Anthropic CEO says AI centralizes by nature and open models just shift power to whoever owns the chips
anthropic_claude_news.summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei argued that AI centralizes power by its nature and that open models simply shift that power to whoever owns the compute. Investor Gavin Baker, former White House adviser David Sacks and Meta's Yann LeCun pushed back publicly on X, accusing him of using risk framing for advantage. Automation angle: know both sides of this argument cold — 'open vs closed models' is the most common opinion question in AI-automation interviews.

anthropic_claude_news.title: How to avoid Claude watermarking your content
anthropic_claude_news.summary: ZDNet walks through where Claude's content-provenance watermarking is applied and how to turn it off for output you intend to publish yourself. It is a small setting most Claude users never find until a downstream tool flags their text. Automation angle: add a provenance/watermark check to any content-generation workflow you ship for a client — silent watermarking is a real deliverability bug.

ai_business_automation.title: Alvys launches AI agents for freight TMS workflows
ai_business_automation.summary: Freight software provider Alvys launched Alvys Foundry, an agentic platform that automates carrier and broker operational tasks inside its existing transportation management system. The agents live where the dispatchers already work rather than in a separate chat product. Automation angle: agents embedded in the system of record beat standalone chatbots — clone this pattern for any vertical SaaS you can get API access to.

ai_business_automation.title: As AI beats doctors, regulators shouldn't force a human into the loop, JAMA piece says
ai_business_automation.summary: A JAMA piece argues that once AI outperforms clinicians on a task, mandating a human in the loop can actively harm patients by dragging results back to the weaker baseline. It reframes human oversight as a cost to be justified, not a default. Automation angle: 'where does the human belong' is the core design question in every automation you will ever ship — this is the strongest published argument on either side.

ai_business_automation.title: Beyond marathons and backflips, China's robots face a commercial test
ai_business_automation.summary: Chinese humanoid and industrial robot makers are moving past demo stunts into deployments that have to return money, with investors at the World Robot Conference focused on payback periods rather than backflips. AI-driven manufacturing automation is entering its prove-the-ROI phase. Automation angle: ROI framing is what closes automation deals — lead every proposal with hours saved per week, not with the model you used.

quantum_ai_research.title: Hybrid Quantum-neural Network Beats Classical Machine Learning - Quantum Zeitgeist
quantum_ai_research.summary: A hybrid quantum-neural network outperformed a classical machine-learning baseline on the same task, with the quantum layer handling the feature transformation and a classical network doing the readout. It is one of the few results where the hybrid actually beats the classical control rather than matching it. Automation angle: hybrid quantum-classical ML is still research-stage — worth reading, not worth building a portfolio piece on yet.

quantum_ai_research.title: Quantinuum, NVIDIA, and Pfizer Validate Generative Quantum AI (GenQAI) Framework for Pharmaceutical R&D - Quantum Computing Report
quantum_ai_research.summary: Quantinuum, NVIDIA and Pfizer validated a Generative Quantum AI (GenQAI) framework for pharmaceutical R&D, using quantum-generated data to train generative models for drug discovery. It is a rare quantum+AI result with a named pharma partner attached. Automation angle: the pattern — quantum hardware generating training data for classical generative models — is the most plausible near-term quantum+AI production path.

quantum_ai_research.title: Nvidia Positions Itself in Hybrid Quantum-Classical Computing with CUDA-Q and Ising Models - News and Statistics - IndexBox
quantum_ai_research.summary: Nvidia is pushing CUDA-Q and Ising-model workloads as the bridge between GPUs and QPUs, positioning its software stack as the default orchestration layer for hybrid quantum-classical AI workloads. Owning the toolchain matters more than owning the qubits. Automation angle: whoever owns the developer toolchain owns the category — the same reason Claude Code matters more than any single model release.

quantum_ai_research.title: A nuclear-quantum-corrected machine-learning potential reveals quantum-enhanced hydrogen segregation at general grain boundaries in alpha-iron
quantum_ai_research.summary: A machine learning interatomic potential corrected for nuclear quantum effects reveals quantum-enhanced hydrogen segregation at grain boundaries in alpha-iron. The neural model makes quantum-accurate simulation tractable at scales direct quantum chemistry cannot reach. Automation angle: 'ML surrogate for an expensive physical simulation' is the most reliably fundable applied-AI pattern in science and engineering.

quantum_ai_research.title: USC researchers use quantum AI to improve cancer imaging - Mugglehead Investment Magazine
quantum_ai_research.summary: USC researchers applied quantum-AI methods to cancer imaging, using quantum-enhanced optimisation to sharpen classification on medical image data. The clinical claims are early but the method is concrete. Automation angle: medical imaging remains the domain where small accuracy gains translate straight into funding — a good area to follow even without quantum hardware.

quantum_ai_research.title: ISRO Experts Highlight AI and Quantum Technology for Future Indian Satellites
quantum_ai_research.summary: ISRO experts outlined AI and quantum technology as the twin pillars for India's next-generation satellite systems at the National Space Technology Conclave 2026, covering onboard autonomy and quantum-secured links. It signals where Indian space R&D funding is going. Automation angle: onboard autonomy is edge-AI under hard constraints — a genuinely differentiated specialisation if you want a niche.

quantum_ai_research.title: QpiAI opens ‘Asia’s largest’ quantum chip foundry, targets 10,000-qubit processors - YourStory.com
quantum_ai_research.summary: Bengaluru-based QpiAI opened what it calls Asia's largest quantum chip foundry, targeting 10,000-qubit processors, and builds AI-driven control and calibration software alongside the hardware. It is India's most substantial quantum+AI infrastructure bet to date. Automation angle: quantum control software is an AI-heavy, under-staffed field — an unusual but real path for someone with strong automation skills.

quantum_ai_research.title: Beyond the Hype: How Hybrid Quantum Computing Is Rewriting the Future of Enterprise AI and Deep Tech - Techloy
quantum_ai_research.summary: An analysis of how hybrid quantum computing is being folded into enterprise AI and deep-tech roadmaps, separating the workloads with real quantum advantage from the ones that are marketing. Optimisation and simulation lead; general ML does not. Automation angle: useful vocabulary for enterprise conversations — knowing which workloads are genuinely quantum-suited stops you nodding along to vendor pitches.

ai_music_copyright_laws.title: Round Hill is suing Suno and Anthropic for up to $1B apiece. It isn’t looking to settle.
ai_music_copyright_laws.summary: Round Hill has filed separate suits against Suno and Anthropic seeking up to $1B apiece, with statutory damages of up to $150,000 per work wilfully infringed. The publisher says it is explicitly not looking to settle, which breaks from how most AI-training suits have ended so far. Automation angle: if you build anything that generates or remixes music, keep a training-data provenance log from day one — it is becoming a procurement requirement.

ai_music_copyright_laws.title: Alibaba launches AI song generator HappyShrimp 1.0 in beta, with China’s Taihe Music signed up for artist co-creation
ai_music_copyright_laws.summary: Alibaba opened a beta of HappyShrimp 1.0, an AI song generator whose prompts control instrumentation, vocal style and how a track's energy shifts across its running time. China's Taihe Music has signed on for artist co-creation, putting a licensed-label deal at the front of the launch rather than after the lawsuit. Automation angle: the licensed-catalogue-first model is the defensible way to build music AI — study this deal structure before pitching any audio-generation product.

elon_musk_ai_vision.title: Try Grok 4.6! Grok 4.7, which is a major upgrade, is coming soon. - x.com
elon_musk_ai_vision.source: Elon Musk on X (via Google News)
elon_musk_ai_vision.summary: Musk publicly pushed users to Grok 4.6 and teased Grok 4.7 as a major upgrade arriving soon, keeping xAI on its roughly monthly release cadence. The pattern is fast, incremental shipping with the announcement made personally on X rather than through a launch post. Automation angle: xAI ships too fast to build a portfolio on — track the cadence for interview small talk, but anchor your demos to the model you can version-pin.

elon_musk_ai_vision.title: Claude Fable 5 vs Grok 4.6 vs DeepSeek V4 [2026] - tech-insider.org
elon_musk_ai_vision.summary: Comparison coverage now benchmarks Grok 4.6 directly against Claude Fable 5 and DeepSeek V4, putting xAI in the same tier conversation as Anthropic and DeepSeek rather than a step behind. Elon's stated position remains that raw capability plus speed wins over safety-first framing. Automation angle: know the deltas well enough to justify your model choice in an interview — 'I picked Claude because X' is a stronger answer than a benchmark table.

unaddressed_ai_problems.title: AI systems quietly drop user instructions when they compress context
unaddressed_ai_problems.summary: A new study shows that when agent frameworks compact long context windows, they silently discard user instructions — the agent keeps running and never signals that a constraint was lost. Anyone operating long-horizon agents is affected, and no mainstream framework surfaces compaction loss to the user. It stays open because compaction is a hidden optimisation, not a documented interface. Automation angle: log every instruction your agent receives and re-assert them after each compaction — a five-line fix that most production agents lack.

unaddressed_ai_problems.title: We still don’t know how people are really using AI
unaddressed_ai_problems.summary: Anthropic and OpenAI publish usage reports, but researchers point out there is no independent measurement of how people actually use these systems — the labs release only what they choose. Policymakers, safety researchers and product teams all plan against numbers they cannot verify. It is unsolved because the only telemetry that exists is proprietary. Automation angle: instrument your own agents properly — a real usage-analytics layer is something you can demo that most AI teams genuinely do not have.

unaddressed_ai_problems.title: Microsoft Copilot reveals secret input that allowed it to be hacked
unaddressed_ai_problems.summary: A secret parameter in Microsoft Copilot let attackers exfiltrate passwords when a target merely clicked a link. It is another prompt-injection-class hole in a shipped enterprise assistant, affecting every organisation with Copilot enabled by default. The category stays open because no vendor has a general defence against injection through untrusted content. Automation angle: never let an agent hold a credential it can be talked into using — scope tokens per action and prove it in your demo.

unaddressed_ai_problems.title: Man Obliterated When Court Obtains His ChatGPT Transcripts
unaddressed_ai_problems.summary: A court obtained a litigant's full ChatGPT transcripts and used them as evidence, a scenario most users have never priced in. Anyone who reasons through personal or legal problems with a chatbot is exposed, and there is no consumer-grade equivalent of privilege or retention control. Nobody is solving it because discovery law moves far slower than adoption. Automation angle: for any client workflow touching sensitive text, default to zero-retention API settings and say so in the proposal — it wins trust immediately.

unaddressed_ai_problems.title: Meta Declines to Remove Horrific Posts Calling for Violence Against Muslims, Calling Them “Cockroaches” and Saying It’s “Time for Hunting”
unaddressed_ai_problems.summary: Meta declined to remove posts calling for violence against Muslims, surfaced amid a flood of AI-generated slop that its moderation systems cannot triage at volume. The affected parties have no escalation path, and the problem persists because generation is now far cheaper than review. Automation angle: high-recall triage classifiers that route to human reviewers are buildable today — this is a real, fundable problem, not a hypothetical one.

ai_business_opportunities.title: ET Graphics: Agentic AI automates retail therapy
ai_business_opportunities.summary: AI agents are now initiating and completing millions of retail transactions weekly — searching products, comparing prices and hunting deals from a chat prompt. Agentic commerce has quietly crossed from demo to volume. **Build:** a merchant-side 'agent readiness' service — structured product feeds, an MCP endpoint and clean pricing data so agents can transact with a store. **For whom:** D2C brands losing traffic to AI shopping assistants. **Why now:** the transactions are already happening and almost no merchant is instrumented for them. Automation angle: ship one merchant MCP server as a public demo — it doubles as the sales pitch.

ai_business_opportunities.title: Partnering with CodeAI to prepare the first AI generation
ai_business_opportunities.summary: OpenAI is partnering with CodeAI to build AI literacy for students — critical thinking about AI plus the skills to use it. Institutional AI education is being bought, not just discussed. **Build:** a cohort-based 'AI automation for non-engineers' program with real n8n/Claude Code builds as the assessment. **For whom:** schools, bootcamps and SMB teams whose staff already use AI badly. **Why now:** the curriculum gap is wider than the tooling gap. Automation angle: your own learning notes are the course — publish the build logs as you go.

ai_business_opportunities.title: China's Lumos eyes fresh funding, potential listing as factory robot sales grow
ai_business_opportunities.summary: China's Lumos has raised about 1 billion yuan ($147M) across seven rounds and is eyeing a listing as sales of its AI-driven factory robots grow, with new capital going to industrial robotics deployments. **Build:** deployment-side automation — the glue between robot fleets, ERP and maintenance ticketing that nobody ships in the box. **For whom:** mid-size manufacturers buying their first robots. **Why now:** hardware is getting cheap faster than the software around it. Automation angle: integration work is where the durable margin sits — position yourself as the layer above the hardware, not beside it.

global_ai_news.title: OpenAI president urges enterprises to hasten AI security defences
global_ai_news.summary: OpenAI president Greg Brockman published an account of the company's joint security work with Hugging Face and warned that enterprise security teams now have a compressed window to adopt AI-based defences. His argument is that attackers are compounding faster than defenders' procurement cycles. Automation angle: an 'AI incident runbook' built in n8n — alert triage, enrichment, human approval gate — is a portfolio piece enterprises actually buy.

global_ai_news.title: Google's AI can see your business data by default in Workspace - unless you disable it
global_ai_news.summary: In Google Workspace, Gemini has default access to Gmail, Docs, Calendar and Chat unless an administrator explicitly disables it. ZDNet lays out what that exposure covers and the exact admin path to turn it off. Automation angle: a 10-minute 'AI data-exposure audit' for small businesses is a genuinely sellable service — Workspace defaults are the easiest first finding.

global_ai_news.title: DOJ probes Andreessen Horowitz over partners sitting on competing AI boards
global_ai_news.summary: The Justice Department is investigating Andreessen Horowitz over partners holding board seats at competing AI companies, a potential Clayton Act interlocking-directorate issue. It is the first serious antitrust look at how concentrated AI cap tables have become. Automation angle: track which funds sit on which boards — overlapping investors is a strong predictor of which AI startups will be hiring next quarter.

global_ai_news.title: The Powerful Chinese AI Model Experts Warned About Is Here
global_ai_news.summary: Z.ai has shipped the frontier Chinese model that security researchers spent months warning about, with cyber-offensive capability strong enough to cut both ways. Wired frames it as a model that could harden company defences or land in attackers' hands with equal ease. Automation angle: open-weight frontier models change your cost model — benchmark one against Claude on a real task before assuming closed models are always the answer.

global_ai_news.title: China's Baidu, betting on AI, posts fifth straight quarterly revenue drop
global_ai_news.summary: Baidu's Q2 revenue fell 4% year-on-year to 31.3 billion yuan ($4.6B), its fifth consecutive quarterly decline, while cash flow still comes mostly from search marketing. The AI pivot is real but has not yet replaced the business it is cannibalising. Automation angle: the classic incumbent trap — study it before you pitch an AI product that competes with a client's own highest-margin line.

global_ai_news.title: Why Apple’s camera-equipped AirPods may not be the ‘pervert pods’ consumers fear
global_ai_news.summary: Apple's leaked camera-equipped AirPods appear to block users from capturing photos or video, feeding the camera only to on-device AI. TechCrunch argues that design choice sidesteps the privacy backlash that hit other AI wearables. Automation angle: 'sensor in, no recording out' is a pattern worth copying in any AI product that touches a customer's environment.

global_ai_news.title: In New Low, Flock CEO Insists His AI-Surveillance Cameras Could Have Solved the Nancy Guthrie Case
global_ai_news.summary: Flock's CEO claimed publicly that his automated licence-plate-reader network could have solved the Nancy Guthrie case, using an unsolved crime to argue for wider camera deployment. The claim is unfalsifiable and drew immediate criticism. Automation angle: watch how AI-surveillance vendors market on counterfactuals — the same rhetorical move shows up in enterprise AI sales decks.

indian_ai_industry.title: Perplexity’s free AI offer left it with millions more users in India
indian_ai_industry.summary: Perplexity's India revenue rose roughly 60% after the free Airtel offer closed to new users, even as download numbers fell. The free tier converted a large enough base that losing top-of-funnel volume did not dent monetisation. Automation angle: this is the clearest recent data point on India's willingness to pay for AI tools — useful if you are pricing an AI service for the Indian market.

indian_ai_industry.title: Peak XV Partners, Together Fund Join Voice AI Unicorn Wispr Flow’s Cap Table
indian_ai_industry.summary: Peak XV Partners and Together Fund have joined the cap table of voice-AI unicorn Wispr Flow. Indian institutional money is now backing voice interfaces as a category rather than a feature. Automation angle: voice-first agents are under-built compared to chat — a Voiceflow or ElevenLabs-MCP voice agent demo stands out sharply in a portfolio right now.

indian_ai_industry.title: Meta Begins Action Against Centre’s Concerns Over CSAM, Deepfakes: Report
indian_ai_industry.summary: Meta has started acting on the Indian government's demands over CSAM and AI-generated deepfakes after what officials called an unequivocal message. IT Ministry sources say the intent is compliance with Indian law rather than censorship, and that action is now visible. Automation angle: India-specific content-moderation compliance is turning into paid automation work — classification pipelines with audit trails are the deliverable.

indian_ai_industry.title: Pepper gives CMOs a way to prove and improve their brand's standing in AI search
indian_ai_industry.summary: Pepper's GEO platform lets chief marketing officers measure and improve how their brand shows up inside AI search answers, a channel with no established analytics layer. It is an early attempt to make generative-engine optimisation reportable to a board. Automation angle: GEO auditing is a wide-open freelance niche — build a scraper that tracks brand mentions across Claude, ChatGPT and Perplexity answers and sell the report.

ai_self_improvement_rsi.title: AI’s recursive self-improvement might not come so quickly after all
ai_self_improvement_rsi.summary: MIT Technology Review pushes back on the industry's boldest claim — that AI will soon improve itself with little human oversight. LLMs already write code, generate synthetic training data and help optimise chips, but the compounding loop those capabilities imply has not materialised. Automation angle: the honest read is that AI accelerates human engineers rather than replacing the loop — which is exactly the job you are training for.

ai_self_improvement_rsi.title: Top AI lab researchers warned about automated AI research, and several of their predicted milestones have already fallen - the-decoder.com
ai_self_improvement_rsi.summary: Researchers at frontier labs published predicted milestones for automated AI research, and several have already been passed. The gap between 'AI helps with research' and 'AI conducts research' is closing faster than the forecasts assumed. Automation angle: read the milestone list and check which ones you can reproduce at small scale — reproducing a lab result is a strong portfolio artefact.

ai_self_improvement_rsi.title: DeepSeek publishes paper on self-evolving AI framework Cordis - KuCoin
ai_self_improvement_rsi.summary: DeepSeek published a paper describing Cordis, a self-evolving AI framework in which the system revises its own strategies across runs rather than being retrained externally. It is one of the few concrete self-improvement architectures with a public write-up. Automation angle: the memory-and-revision loop generalises to ordinary agents — persist what failed and feed it back next run.

ai_self_improvement_rsi.title: Improving the matrix multiplication exponent with modern optimization and AlphaEvolve
ai_self_improvement_rsi.summary: AlphaEvolve, combined with modern optimisation, improved the known exponent for matrix multiplication — an AI system producing a genuine advance on a decades-old open problem in algorithms. This is AI doing AI-relevant research, not assisting it. Automation angle: evolutionary search over generated candidates plus a hard verifier is a pattern you can copy on any problem where correctness is cheap to check.

ai_self_improvement_rsi.title: AutoSR: Automatic Symbolic Regression by Searching Research States
ai_self_improvement_rsi.summary: AutoSR automates symbolic regression by searching over research states rather than equations directly, letting the AI decide what to investigate next. It is an automated-science loop with the hypothesis-selection step moved inside the model itself. Automation angle: 'search over research states' is the same shape as an agent planning its own next tool call — a useful mental model for agent design.

ai_self_improvement_rsi.title: Historical Backtesting for Scientific Question Discovery: A Protocol and Astronomy Pilot
ai_self_improvement_rsi.summary: A protocol for backtesting AI-generated scientific questions against history — asking whether a system would have posed the right question before the answer was known — piloted on astronomy. It gives automated-research claims a falsifiable evaluation. Automation angle: backtesting an agent against past decisions is the cheapest honest eval you can build, in science or in business workflows.

ai_model_benchmarks.title: Text / LLM - Best: Claude Opus 5 / Runner-up: GPT-5.x
ai_model_benchmarks.summary: Current category leader: Claude Opus 5; runner-up GPT-5.x. Automation angle: switch your portfolio demos to whichever model ranks best in the category you build in this week.

ai_model_benchmarks.title: Reading Zhipu’s GLM-5.3 results past the headline number
ai_model_benchmarks.summary: Zhipu's own GLM-5.3 release note contains a line most coverage skipped: the company says its cybersecurity capability is growing faster than it expected. The headline benchmark number is the least interesting part of the release. Automation angle: always read the release note itself, not the recap — the caveats vendors bury are what actually affects your build.

ai_model_benchmarks.title: Qwen 3.8 27B scores 52 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index
ai_model_benchmarks.summary: Qwen 3.8 27B scores 52 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, matching models several times its size. Simon Willison notes it as another step in open-weight models closing the gap at small parameter counts. Automation angle: a 27B model that scores like a frontier one runs on hardware you can rent cheaply — worth benchmarking for the bulk steps in your pipelines.

ai_model_benchmarks.title: Diagnosing Dense Same-Class Attribute Misbinding in Large Vision-Language Models
ai_model_benchmarks.summary: Vision-language models can identify every object and attribute in a crowded scene yet bind an attribute to the wrong instance of the same class — a failure generic VQA accuracy completely hides. The paper proposes a targeted diagnostic instead. Automation angle: if your workflow reads images, test same-class binding explicitly; aggregate accuracy will not catch this failure.

new_ai_tools.title: Warp’s new system is an out-of-the-box software factory for AI development
new_ai_tools.summary: Warp launched Warp Factories, infrastructure that stands up an AI 'software factory' — parallel coding agents with shared context and review gates — without assembling the stack yourself. It targets exactly the multi-agent orchestration most solo builders hand-roll. Automation angle: try it against your Claude Code workflow this week and publish the comparison; head-to-head agent-harness reviews are under-produced content.

new_ai_tools.title: Firefox’s Smart Window promises a better AI browser
new_ai_tools.summary: Firefox's Smart Window mode can now pull live web results and show source links inside AI chat responses through a partnership with Exa, plus auto-suggest tabs. It is the first mainstream browser AI mode with a real citation layer. Automation angle: Exa's API is the retrieval piece here — swap it into your RAG demo and you get grounded, link-backed answers without building an index.

new_ai_tools.title: OpenAI launches a ChatGPT version built for teens
new_ai_tools.summary: OpenAI shipped ChatGPT for Teens for 13-17 year olds, bundling existing minor safeguards with study mode, quiet hours and parental account linking. Most protections already existed; the launch consolidates them under one product amid legal pressure. Automation angle: age-gating and parental controls are becoming table stakes — if you build an AI product touching under-18 users, copy this control set.

new_ai_tools.title: I tested Omarchy Quattro, one of the first Linux distros to go all in on AI - and I didn't hate it
new_ai_tools.summary: ZDNet tested Omarchy Quattro, one of the first Linux distributions built around AI tooling as a first-class part of the desktop rather than an add-on. The reviewer expected to hate it and did not. Automation angle: an AI-native dev environment is a cheap differentiator — a 'my AI-first terminal setup' video is reliable channel content.

general_news.title: Zambia's Hichilema re-elected president as main rival in hiding over alleged threats
general_news.summary: Hakainde Hichilema has been re-elected president of Zambia, saying he was "truly humbled" and promising to govern for all Zambians. His main rival is in hiding, alleging threats against him, which leaves the result contested in practice if not on paper.

general_news.title: Pakistan top court orders ex-PM Imran Khan be moved to hospital from jail
general_news.summary: Pakistan's supreme court has ordered former prime minister Imran Khan moved from jail to hospital. Khan has been imprisoned since 2023 on corruption charges he maintains were politically motivated.

general_news.title: UAE Warns Of 'Potential Missile Threats', Asks People To Seek Shelter
general_news.summary: The UAE issued a public warning over potential missile threats and told residents to seek shelter. The alert came a day after the memorandum of understanding between Iran and the United States expired.

general_news.title: Disney and ABC sue Trump's media regulator to stop early licence renewal
general_news.summary: Disney and ABC are suing the Trump administration's media regulator to block an early licence renewal review. The network says the move is retaliation because the administration "disapproves of what ABC broadcasts".

general_news.title: Kariba ferry death toll rises to 93, making it Zimbabwe's deadliest transport disaster
general_news.summary: The death toll from the Kariba ferry disaster has risen to 93, making it Zimbabwe's deadliest transport disaster on record. Recovery operations are still under way.

general_news.title: UK 'supports Ukraine 100%', Burnham says, after Russia's drone warning
general_news.summary: Russia has accused the UK of escalating the war in Ukraine by supplying British-made drones, prompting Andy Burnham to say the UK backs Ukraine "100%". The prime minister has vowed to support Kyiv in its "hour of need".

general_news.title: Brazil's President Lula hails oil discovery near Amazon river
general_news.summary: President Lula has celebrated a significant oil discovery near the mouth of the Amazon river. Environmental groups have sharply criticised the exploratory drilling in those waters.

general_news.title: El Nino Accelerates Rapidly, Could Become Strongest On Record, Experts Warn
general_news.summary: Forecasters warn the current El Nino is strengthening rapidly and could become the strongest on record. At those levels it reshapes weather systems worldwide, from monsoon timing to Atlantic storm activity.
